official.description_text:
Postdoc in Nuclear Engineering
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences
Job description
We are looking for a postdoctoral fellow to work on development of experimental methods for two-phase flows. We aim to develop a probe for measurement of void fraction and velocity at prototypic reactor conditions. The work includes development of methods for manufacturing miniature sensors and using these sensors in the HWAT facility. The HWAT facility was developed to study thermohydraulic phenomena relevant to small modular reactors (SMRs). The work is a part of a collaborative project in Europe and national project supported by Swedish nuclear regulator (SSM).
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Doctoral degree in experimental nuclear engineering, micro-mechanics, sol-gel chemistry, experimental thermohydraulics.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Knowledge and experience of experimental investigation of two-phase flows, sol-gel coating, micro-mechanical manufacturing, high frequency signal processing.
Good communication and collaborative skills, capability to work in a team and independently.
Motivation and dedication to research work is a very strong merit.
Teaching experience is an advantage.
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
your application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of your academic interests and how this project relates to your future goals, why you would be the best candidate to work on the project. Maximally two pages long.
Letters of support, if at hand, or contact details for 2-3 reference persons.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position at KTH focused on experimental methods for two-phase flows in small modular reactors, involving sensor manufacturing and thermohydraulic testing in the HWAT facility. Part of European and Swedish national nuclear research projects.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position core is experimental nuclear engineering and thermohydraulics—pure engineering domain with no human-centred, HCI, learning, or immersive systems dimensions. The researcher's entire profile (spatial cognition, collaborative learning, XR design, wayfinding, user studies) is orthogonal to nuclear sensor development and two-phase flow measurement.

methodological_fit.rationale: Researcher has experimental design and quantitative research skills, which are present in nuclear work. However, the experimental context (sensor manufacturing, high-frequency signal processing, thermohydraulics instrumentation) requires domain expertise in micro-mechanics, sol-gel chemistry, and physics—not HCI methodology. No overlap in research methods or tools.

growth_value.rationale: This position would close zero gaps aligned with the researcher's target identity (human-centred XR, collaborative systems, spatial learning). Instead, it would redirect toward experimental physics and engineering, moving further from doctoral HCI research goals.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a strong institution with stable European and national funding. However, this group's research agenda (nuclear thermohydraulics) is disconnected from the researcher's target institutions (Aalto, TU Delft) and their HCI/immersive systems communities. Limited value for building a human-centred XR research network.

eligibility_flags: Researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress, thesis stage); position requires completed doctoral degree by employment decision. Not yet eligible.
Position may require security clearance under Swedish Protective Security Act; eligibility depends on nationality and clearance approval—nationality not stated in profile.
risks: Fundamental domain mismatch: nuclear engineering ≠ HCI. Accepting would delay PhD entry and diverge from target identity.
No immersive systems, user research, or learning science component.
Researcher is not yet PhD-eligible; position is postdoctoral.
Research group and institution focus is engineering-physics, not human-centred design or HCI.
Security clearance requirement may introduce barriers.
